paragraphs: We are a late-stage clinical biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing cretostimogene grenadenorepvec (cretostimogene), an investigational oncolytic immunotherapy with a dual mechanism of action designed both to eliminate cancer cells directly by selective replication and indirectly by activating an anti-tumor immune response, as a potential backbone therapy in a broad range of patients afflicted with bladder cancer. Cretostimogene is currently in clinical development for the treatment of patients with high-risk and intermediate-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC), which potentially represents up to 150,000 addressable patients.

We are evaluating the safety and efficacy of cretostimogene as a monotherapy in BOND-003 Cohort C, our ongoing Phase 3 clinical trial in high-risk Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG)-unresponsive NMIBC with carcinoma in situ (CIS), with or without Ta/T1 disease. Given the limitations of currently approved therapies, the next course of treatment for these patients with BCG-unresponsive tumors is radical cystectomy, which is the complete removal of the bladder. This surgery carries a significant social, functional and emotional burden for patients. As such, there is a significant unmet need for effective bladder-sparing treatments. We have completed enrollment for this cohort and reported potentially best-in-disease data in September 2025. This trial served as the basis for our Biologics License Application (BLA) submission for our initial indication to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which we initiated in the fourth quarter of 2025 and expect to complete in 2026. Cretostimogene has received both Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations from the FDA for the treatment of high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS with or without Ta or T1 papillary tumors. Additionally, in April 2024, we initiated BOND-003 Cohort P, an exploratory study evaluating cretostimogene monotherapy in high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with only Ta/T1 disease. Initial data from this Cohort was reported at the 2025 AUA Annual Meeting, with potentially best-in-disease data reported at the Society of Urologic Oncology (SUO) 26th Annual Meeting in December 2025. Based on internal research derived from the National Cancer Institute Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program's (NIH SEER) database, secondary claims data analytics and management assumptions, the high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC segment may represent up to 25,000 addressable patients.

We are also conducting a Phase 3 clinical trial, PIVOT-006, the first randomized registrational trial to evaluate an investigational therapy in intermediate-risk NMIBC assessing adjuvant cretostimogene following transurethral resection of the bladder tumor (TURBT), with enrollment completed in the third quarter of 2025. These patients with intermediate-risk NMIBC are encumbered by frequent tumor recurrence that requires repeat resection of the bladder tumors. Moreover, intravesical BCG is no longer recommended by guidelines for this patient population due to the continuous BCG shortage. We believe cretostimogene, if approved in intermediate-risk NMIBC, has the potential to serve as a first-in-class backbone therapy in this frontline adjuvant setting, for which there are currently no U.S. FDA approved options. Based on internal research derived from NIH SEER database, secondary claims data analytics and management assumptions, the intermediate-risk NMIBC segment may represent up to 50,000 addressable patients.

Additionally, we have multiple ongoing Phase 2 cohorts designed to generate data in high-risk BCG-exposed and BCG-naïve patients. In October 2024, we initiated CORE-008 Cohort A, a Phase 2 clinical trial in high-risk NMIBC patients who are naïve to BCG treatment, including patients with CIS and with or without Ta/T1 disease and patients with only Ta/T1 disease. Initial data from this Cohort were reported at the SUO Annual Meeting in December 2025. Based on internal research derived from NIH SEER database, secondary claims data analytics and management assumptions, the high-risk BCG-naïve NMIBC segment may represent up to 25,000 addressable patients. In March 2025, we expanded CORE-008 evaluating cretostimogene as a monotherapy in the high-risk BCG-exposed population (Cohort B). In addition, in April 2025, we initiated a third Cohort (Cohort CX), evaluating cretostimogene in combination with gemcitabine in both the high-risk BCG-exposed and BCG-unresponsive population. Based on internal research derived from NIH SEER database, secondary claims data analytics and management assumptions, the high-risk BCG-exposed NMIBC segment may represent up to 50,000 addressable patients. Notably, cretostimogene's potential for combination with other therapies was assessed in a Phase 2 CORE-001 clinical trial evaluating cretostimogene in combination with the checkpoint inhibitor (CPI) pembrolizumab in high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC patients.

We intend to develop a potentially category-defining, bladder-sparing therapeutic for patients afflicted with bladder cancer by evaluating cretostimogene for use in a broad range of bladder cancer indications, as shown in our pipeline below.

We believe our product candidate, cretostimogene, has a potential best-in-disease target product profile that supports our vision of cretostimogene as a potential backbone bladder-sparing therapy in bladder cancer. The key differentiating factors include:

• Favorable monotherapy data. Cretostimogene demonstrated sustained, durable complete responses in high-risk BCG-unresponsive NMIBC, with a 75.5% CR at any time, and 46.4% of evaluable responders maintaining their response for at least 12 months and 41.8% at 24 months (CR rate observed in 46 out of 110 patients). This topline data shows that 90% of 12-month responders remain disease free at two years, as of June 23, 2025 cutoff in our Phase 3 BOND-003 Cohort C trial. The estimated 12- and 24-month duration of response (DOR) rates are 64.1% and 58.3%, respectively. Median DOR is 28 months and is ongoing.

• Strong safety and tolerability profile. No Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were observed and no patient discontinued cretostimogene due to TRAEs as of June 23, 2025 cutoff in our Phase 3 BOND-003 Cohort C trial. The median time to TRAE resolution was one day. No treatment-related discontinuation of cretostimogene was observed, and 97.3% of patients completed all expected treatments, demonstrating favorable patient adherence and compliance. The most common TRAEs (≥10%) were bladder spasm, pollakiuria, micturition urgency, dysuria, and hematuria.

• Simple route of administration. Similar to the standard-of-care BCG therapy, cretostimogene is administered intravesically without changing practice workflow, and urology practices perform intravesical procedures regularly. This is unlike some treatment procedures that require a urologist to perform a cystoscopic examination that involves local anesthesia.

• Potential for combination with other therapies. Cretostimogene, in combination with the CPI pembrolizumab produced an 82.9% CR at any time in our completed Phase 2 CORE-001 clinical trial, with no Grade 3 or higher TRAEs attributable to cretostimogene, demonstrating the potential benefits of using cretostimogene in a combination therapy. Cretostimogene's combination potential is being further assessed in a Phase 2 CORE-008 Cohort CX clinical trial evaluating cretostimogene in combination with gemcitabine in high-risk BCG-exposed and BCG-unresponsive NMIBC patients.

• Potential broad applicability across bladder cancer indications. Due to its novel dual mechanisms of action, cretostimogene has the potential to address a broad range of bladder cancer indications, including high-risk BCG-naïve, exposed and unresponsive NMIBC, as well as intermediate-risk NMIBC. Cretostimogene has the potential to be a first-in-class adjuvant therapy for patients with intermediate-risk NMIBC in the broadest label by AUO/SUO guideline definition that includes those with solitary high-grade Ta disease less than or equal to 3 cm in size. These patients are encumbered by frequent tumor recurrence that requires repeat resection of the bladder tumors. Also, there is incremental opportunity in muscle invasive bladder cancer (MIBC).

Bladder cancer is a heterogeneous disease and involves a number of different cancer stages, which can be segmented into NMIBC or MIBC. The American Cancer Society estimates that in 2026, approximately 85,000 people will be diagnosed with bladder cancer and that the disease will result in nearly 17,900 deaths. An estimated 730,000 people in the United States are currently living with the disease. NMIBC, which accounts for approximately 75% of newly diagnosed patients, describes earlier-stage bladder cancer that has not spread to the muscle wall. NMIBC can be further stratified by its specific risk profile, with high-risk NMIBC making up approximately 40% of the NMIBC patient population, at an elevated probability of disease progression to more aggressive MIBC within five years of initial diagnosis. Patients with intermediate-risk disease account for approximately 30% of total NMIBC diagnoses.

Current treatment for high-risk NMIBC typically involves TURBT followed by the intravesical (IVE) delivery of BCG therapy to induce an anti-tumor immune response. This treatment protocol has demonstrated therapeutic benefit with nearly 70% of patients achieving a CR following an initial induction course of therapy. However, approximately 50% of these patients will experience a recurrence of the tumor and few treatment options are available for patients whose disease becomes unresponsive to BCG treatment. While radical cystectomy is the current guideline recommended treatment for BCG-unresponsive NMIBC, only approximately 6% of patients with NMIBC elect to undergo cystectomy considering the significant social, functional and emotional burden associated with this procedure. Further complicating the treatment options available to patients with NMIBC is the ongoing shortage of BCG which has restricted patient eligibility to high-risk BCG-naïve NMIBC. Even among these patients a significant number of newly diagnosed, BCG-eligible, treatment-naïve patients in the United States may not receive sufficient BCG therapy, if at all. Moreover, patients with intermediate-risk NMIBC may not have access to BCG due to the shortage, despite the likely therapeutic benefit of earlier adjuvant BCG therapy, because high-risk patients are prioritized in line with guidance published by the National Comprehensive Care Network (NCCN) and guidance published jointly by the American Urological Association (AUA) and the SUO. Although intermediate-risk patients have lower risk of progression, this patient population is the most heterogeneous of all risk categories, comprising of mostly multifocal or frequently recurring low-grade lesions or high-grade Ta lesions less than 3 cm that are frequently refractory to current intravesical treatments. Therefore, the standard of care for management is centered on surgical removal of visible lesions via TURBT, which places similarly functional and emotional burden on intermediate-risk patients who experience frequent invasive surgery to minimize repeat disease recurrence.

Instances of refractory and recurrent disease, patient aversion to cystectomy and the ongoing BCG supply constraints, have created a sizeable unmet medical need for alternative NMIBC therapeutics that are both safe and efficacious. In addition to our registrational clinical trials in both high-risk and intermediate-risk NMIBC, we also initiated CORE-008, an open-label, multi-arm, multi-cohort Phase 2 clinical trial designed to assess the safety and efficacy of cretostimogene when administered as monotherapy in high-risk BCG-exposed and BCG-naïve NMIBC patients, as well as in combination in high-risk BCG-exposed and BCG-unresponsive NMIBC patients. BCG-exposed patients are classified as those with persistent, recurrent or progressive disease after BCG treatment but who do not meet the specific disease classification criteria requisite to be designated as BCG-unresponsive. BCG-naïve NMIBC is classified as patients who have not received any prior BCG therapy.

headings: Risks Related to the Development and Regulatory Approval of Our Product Candidates

Cretostimogene is based on a novel approach to the treatment of cancer, which makes it difficult to predict the time and cost of product candidate development and subsequently obtaining regulatory approval, if at all.
We have not as an organization completed submission of a BLA, and we may be unable to do so for cretostimogene or any future product candidates.
We are developing cretostimogene in combination with other therapies, which exposes us to additional risks.
Changes in methods of the manufacturing or formulation of cretostimogene or any future product candidates may result in additional costs or delay.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risk factors, together with the other information contained in this Annual Report, including our consolidated financial statements and the related notes and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," before making an investment decision regarding our securities. We cannot assure you that any of the events discussed in the risk factors below will not occur. These risks could have a material and adverse impact on our business, results of operations, financial condition and growth prospects. If that were to happen, the trading price of our common stock could decline. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations or financial condition. In this section, we first provide a summary of the principal risks and uncertainties we face and then provide a full set of risk factors and discuss them in greater detail.

We currently depend entirely on the success of cretostimogene, which is our only product candidate. If we are unable to advance cretostimogene in clinical development, obtain regulatory approval and ultimately commercialize cretostimogene, or experience significant delays in doing so, our business will be materially harmed.

We currently only have one product candidate, cretostimogene, which is in Phase 3 clinical development. Our business presently depends entirely on our ability to successfully develop, obtain regulatory approval for, and commercialize cretostimogene in a timely manner. This may make an investment in our company riskier than similar companies that have multiple product candidates in active development and may be able to better sustain the delay or failure of a lead product candidate. The success of cretostimogene will depend on several factors, including the following:

• successful initiation and enrollment of clinical trials and completion of clinical trials with favorable results, including the full data readouts from the ongoing Phase 3 clinical trials for cretostimogene;

• acceptance of regulatory submissions by the U.S. FDA or comparable foreign regulatory authorities for the conduct of clinical trials of cretostimogene and of our proposed designs of planned clinical trials of cretostimogene;
• the frequency and severity of adverse events observed in clinical trials and preclinical studies;

Since our inception in 2010, we have focused substantially all of our resources on organizing and staffing our company, business planning, raising capital, establishing and maintaining our intellectual property portfolio, conducting research, preclinical studies, and clinical trials, establishing arrangements with third parties for the manufacture of cretostimogene, and providing general and administrative support for these operations. We do not have any products approved for sale and have not generated any revenue from product sales.

We have incurred significant operating losses and negative cash flows from operations since our inception. Our net losses were $161.0 million and $88.0 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $379.0 million. Substantially all of our net losses have resulted from costs incurred in connection with our research and development programs and, to a lesser extent, from general and administrative costs associated with our operations. We expect to continue to incur significant expenses and operating losses in the foreseeable future, and we anticipate these losses will increase substantially as we continue our development of, seek regulatory approval for, and potentially commercialize cretostimogene and potentially seek to discover and develop additional product candidates, utilize third parties to manufacture cretostimogene, hire additional personnel, expand and protect our intellectual property, and incur additional costs associated with being a public company. If we obtain regulatory approval for cretostimogene, we expect to incur significant expenses related to developing our commercialization capability to support product sales, marketing and distribution. Because of the numerous risks and uncertainties associated with pharmaceutical product development, we are unable to accurately predict the timing or amount of increased expenses or when, or if, we will be able to achieve or maintain profitability. Even if we are able to generate product sales, we may not become profitable. If we do not become profitable or are unable to sustain profitability on a continuing basis, then we may be unable to continue our operations at planned levels and may be forced to reduce or terminate our operations.

To date, we have primarily funded our operations with proceeds from the sale of shares of our common stock through public offerings and our redeemable convertible preferred stock, as well as through previously outstanding term debt. In January 2024, we completed our initial public offering of 23,000,000 common shares at a price of $19.00 per share, including the exercise in full by the underwriters of their option to purchase an additional 3,000,000 shares of common stock. We received net proceeds of $399.6 million, after deducting discounts, commissions and other offering expenses. In addition, as a result of our initial public offering, our convertible preferred stock converted into common stock concurrently with the initial public offering. In December 2024, we completed a follow-on offering of 8,500,000 common shares at a price of $28.00 per share, including the exercise in full by the underwriters of their option to purchase an additional 1,200,000 shares of common stock. We received net proceeds of $223.1 million, after deducting discounts, commissions and other offering expenses. On March 28, 2025, we entered into an Open Market Sale AgreementSM (Jefferies Sales Agreement) with Jefferies LLC, as agent, pursuant to which we may offer and sell, from time to time through Jefferies, shares of our common stock. On the same day, we filed a shelf registration statement on Form S-3ASR with the SEC, which contains a base prospectus, covering an unlimited amount of our common stock, preferred stock, debt securities and warrants to purchase any of such securities, and a sales agreement prospectus, which we subsequently amended on January 13, 2026, covering the offering, issuance and sale of up to a maximum aggregate offering price of $550 million of our common stock that may be issued and sold from time to time under the Jefferies Sales Agreement. Through December 31, 2025, the Company received net proceeds of $147.1 million under the Jefferies Sales Agreement, after deducting discounts and commissions and other offering expenses. Subsequent to December 31, 2025, the Company received net proceeds of $188.0 million under the Jefferies Sales Agreement, after deducting discounts and commissions.

Through December 31, 2025, we have received aggregate gross proceeds of approximately $1.1 billion from the sale of shares of our common stock from our IPO, our follow-on offering in December 2024, and our at-the-market facility, and sales of our redeemable convertible preferred stock. In addition, through December 31, 2025, we have recognized $26.9 million in license and collaboration revenue pursuant to our license and collaboration agreements. As of December 31, 2025, we had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $742.2 million, which excludes $188.0 million of net cash proceeds received by the Company from the sale of 3,623,101 shares under the Jefferies Sales Agreement subsequent to December 31, 2025. Our ability to generate any product revenue and, in particular, our ability to generate product revenue sufficient to achieve profitability, will depend on the successful development and eventual commercialization of cretostimogene and any future product candidates.

In February 2025, the Company's wholly owned subsidiary, SafeGuard Healthcare, LLC (SafeGuard), established a note receivable with an initial principal amount of $25.0 million through a convertible promissory note (Note) from SP Healthcare SPV I, LLC (the SPV). The SPV used the proceeds from the Note to make an investment in Biovire for the purpose of Biovire acquiring substantially all of the assets of a contract manufacturing organization that provides clinical supply of cretostimogene to the Company. On July 20, 2025, following the conversion of the Note triggered by the cessation of services by SkyPath to the SPV and Biovire (Conversion Event), we, through our subsidiary, SafeGuard, obtained control of the SPV and Biovire. As a result of this change in control, the operations of Biovire were consolidated as of the effective date of the conversion.

We believe, based on our current operating plan, that our existing cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, will be sufficient to fund our operations for at least the next twelve months from the date of this Annual Report. However, we have based this estimate on assumptions that may prove to be wrong, and our operating plan may change as a result of many factors currently unknown to us. In addition, we could utilize our available capital resources sooner than we expect.

We will not generate revenue from product sales of cretostimogene or any future product candidates unless and until we successfully complete clinical development and obtain regulatory approval, which we expect will take a number of years and may never occur. As a result, we will need substantial additional funding to support our continuing operations and pursue our growth strategy. Until such time as we can generate significant revenue from product sales, if ever, we expect to finance our operations through equity offerings, debt financings, or other capital sources, including current or potential future collaborations, licenses, and other similar arrangements. However, we may be unable to raise additional funds or enter into such other agreements or arrangements when needed on favorable terms, or at all. If we fail to raise capital or enter into such agreements or arrangements as, and when needed, we may delay, limit, reduce or terminate our product development or future commercialization efforts or grant rights to develop and market product candidates that we would otherwise prefer to develop and market ourselves, or even cease operations.

Other than Biovire, which manufactures and conducts release testing of our cretostimogene drug product, we do not own or operate, and currently have no plans to establish, any manufacturing facilities. We rely, and expect to continue to rely, on Biovire and third parties for the manufacture of cretostimogene for clinical testing, as well as for commercial manufacture if we obtain marketing approval. In addition, we rely on third parties to package, label, store, and distribute cretostimogene, and we intend to rely on third parties for our commercial products if marketing approval is obtained. We believe that this strategy allows us to maintain a more efficient infrastructure by eliminating the need for us to invest in our own manufacturing facilities, equipment, and personnel while also enabling us to focus our expertise and resources on the development of cretostimogene.

Cretostimogene 單獨療法用於高風險 NMIBC
paragraphs: 本公司為一家晚期臨牀生物製藥公司，專注於開發與商業化創傷性刺激素基因重組病毒（cretostimogene grenadenorepvec，cretostimogene），一種正在研究中的腫瘤免疫療法，具有雙重作用機制，設計用以直接透過選擇性複製消除癌細胞，並間接透過活化抗腫瘤免疫反應，作為治療廣泛膀胱癌患者的潛在基礎療法。cretostimogene 目前正在臨牀開發中，用於治療高風險及中風險非肌肉侵襲性膀胱癌（NMIBC）患者，這類患者潛在可治療人數可能達 15 萬人。

本公司正在評估 cretostimogene 作為單一療法在 BOND-003 羣組 C 的安全性與有效性，這是我們持續進行的第三期臨牀試驗，針對高風險巴氏桿菌卡介苗（BCG）無反應性 NMIBC 並伴有原位癌（CIS）的患者，無論是否同時患有 Ta/T1 病變。考慮到目前核准療法的限制，這些 BCG 無反應性腫瘤患者的下一步治療為根治性膀胱切除術，即完全移除膀胱。此手術對患者而言具有顯著的社會、功能與情感負擔。因此，對於有效的膀胱保留治療，存在顯著未滿足的醫療需求。我們已完成此羣組的招募，並於 2025 年 9 月報告了潛在最佳療效的數據。此試驗成為我們向美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）提交生物製品許可申請（BLA）的基礎，我們於 2025 年第四季啟動此申請，預計於 2026 年完成。cretostimogene 已獲得 FDA 對治療高風險 BCG 無反應性 NMIBC 並伴有 CIS 且無 Ta 或 T1 腫瘤的快速通道與突破性療法認可。此外，於 2024 年 4 月，我們啟動了 BOND-003 羣組 P，這是一項探索性研究，評估 cretostimogene 單一療法在高風險 BCG 無反應性 NMIBC 並僅有 Ta/T1 病變患者的療效。此羣組的初步數據於 2025 年 AUA 年度會議報告，潛在最佳療效數據於 2025 年 12 月 Society of Urologic Oncology（SUO）第 26 屆年度會議報告。根據內部研究，來自國家癌症研究所監測、流行病學與結果計劃（NIH SEER）資料庫、次級主張數據分析與管理假設，高風險 BCG 無反應性 NMIBC 羣組可能代表最多 25,000 名可治療患者。

我們同時進行一項第三期臨牀試驗，PIVOT-006，這是首個隨機註冊試驗，評估一種正在研究的療法在中風險 NMIBC 患者中的療效，評估在經尿道膀胱腫瘤切除術（TURBT）後使用 cretostimogene 作為輔助治療，招募工作於 2025 年第三季完成。這些中風險 NMIBC 患者因頻繁腫瘤復發而需重複進行膀胱腫瘤切除手術。此外，由於持續的 BCG 短缺，目前指南已不再建議此患者羣體使用經膀胱 BCG 治療。我們認為，若 cretostimogene 在中風險 NMIBC 中獲准，將有潛力成為此一前線輔助治療環境中的首個療法，目前尚無美國 FDA 核准的選擇。根據內部研究，來自 NIH SEER 資料庫、次級主張數據分析與管理假設，中風險 NMIBC 羣組可能代表最多 50,000 名可治療患者。

此外，我們有多項進行中的第二期試驗，旨在產生高風險 BCG 曾接觸與未接觸患者的數據。於 2024 年 10 月，我們啟動了 CORE-008 羣組 A，這是一項第二期臨牀試驗，針對未曾接觸 BCG 治療的高風險 NMIBC 患者，包括患有 CIS 且有或無 Ta/T1 病變的患者，以及僅有 Ta/T1 病變的患者。此羣組的初步數據於 2025 年 12 月 SUO 年度會議報告。根據內部研究，來自 NIH SEER 資料庫、次級主張數據分析與管理假設，高風險 BCG 未接觸 NMIBC 羣組可能代表最多 25,000 名可治療患者。於 2025 年 3 月，我們擴展了 CORE-008，評估 cretostimogene 單一療法在高風險 BCG 曾接觸患者（羣組 B）中的療效。此外，於 2025 年 4 月，我們啟動了第三個羣組（羣組 CX），評估 cretostimogene 與吉西他濱聯合使用在高風險 BCG 曾接觸與 BCG 無反應性患者中的療效。根據內部研究，來自 NIH SEER 資料庫、次級主張數據分析與管理假設，高風險 BCG 曾接觸 NMIBC 羣組可能代表最多 50,000 名可治療患者。值得注意的是，cretostimogene 與其他療法組合的潛力已在第二期 CORE-001 臨牀試驗中評估，該試驗評估 cretostimogene 與檢查點抑制劑（CPI）帕博利珠單抗在高風險 BCG 無反應性 NMIBC 患者中的組合療效。
我們計畫開發一種可能定義該類別的膀胱保留療法，用以治療患有膀胱癌的患者，評估 cretostimogene 在廣泛膀胱癌適應症中的應用，如我們的產品管道所示。
我們認為我們的產品候選藥物 cretostimogene 具有潛在的最佳療效產品特性，支持我們將 cretostimogene 視為膀胱癌中可能的基礎膀胱保留療法的願景。關鍵的差異因素包括：

• 有利的單一療法數據。cretostimogene 在高風險 BCG 無反應性 NMIBC 中顯示出持續且持久的完全反應，其任何時間點的完全反應率為 75.5%，且 46.4% 的可評估反應者維持反應至少 12 個月，41.8% 維持反應至少 24 個月（在 110 名患者中觀察到 46 名完全反應者）。此初步數據顯示，在我們第三期 BOND-003 羣組 C 試驗中，截至 2025 年 6 月 23 日的截止日期，90% 的 12 個月反應者在兩年後仍保持無病狀態。預估的 12 個月與 24 個月反應持續時間（DOR）率分別為 64.1% 與 58.3%，中位數 DOR 為 28 個月，且仍在進行中。

• 強大的安全性與耐受性。截至 2025 年 6 月 23 日的截止日期，在我們第三期 BOND-003 羣組 C 試驗中，未觀察到 Grade 3 或更高程度的治療相關不良事件（TRAEs），也無患者因 TRAEs 而中止 cretostimogene 治療。TRAEs 解決的中位數時間為一天。未觀察到因 TRAEs 而中止 cretostimogene 治療的情況，且 97.3% 的患者完成所有預期治療，顯示出良好的患者依從性與順從性。最常見的 TRAEs（≥10%）為膀胱痙攣、頻尿、排尿急迫、排尿疼痛與血尿。
• 簡單的給藥途徑。與標準療法 BCG 治療類似，cretostimogene 是經由膀胱內給藥，不改變現有醫療作業流程，泌尿科醫療機構定期執行膀胱內手術。這與一些需要泌尿科醫師執行膀胱鏡檢查並使用局部麻醉的治療程序不同。

• 與其他療法組合使用的潛力。cretostimogene 與 CPI pembrolizumab 組合，在我們已完成的 Phase 2 CORE-001 臨牀試驗中，達到 82.9% 的完全緩解率（CR），且無 Grade 3 或以上與 cretostimogene 相關的不良事件（TRAEs），顯示使用 cretostimogene 進行組合療法的潛在好處。cretostimogene 的組合潛力正在 Phase 2 CORE-008 Cohort CX 臨牀試驗中進一步評估，該試驗評估 cretostimogene 與 gemcitabine 組合在高風險 BCG 曝露及 BCG 未反應 NMIBC 患者中的應用。

• 潛在廣泛適用於膀胱癌各類別。由於其新型雙重作用機制，cretostimogene 有潛力應對廣泛的膀胱癌類別，包括高風險 BCG 未接觸、曝露及未反應 NMIBC，以及中風險 NMIBC。cretostimogene 有潛力成為中風險 NMIBC 患者的首個類別治療藥物，根據 AUO/SUO 指南定義，這類患者包括單一高級 Ta 病變且大小小於或等於 3 公分的患者。這些患者因頻繁腫瘤復發而需重複切除膀胱腫瘤。此外，在肌肉侵襲性膀胱癌（MIBC）中也存在進一步的治療機會。

膀胱癌是一種異質性疾病，涉及多種不同的癌症階段，可分為 NMIBC 或 MIBC。美國癌症協會預估，2026 年將約有 85,000 人被診斷出患有膀胱癌，且該疾病將導致近 17,900 人死亡。美國目前約有 730,000 人正在與該疾病共存。NMIBC，約佔新診斷患者的 75%，描述的是尚未擴散至肌肉壁的早期階段膀胱癌。NMIBC 可進一步根據其特定風險特徵進行分層，其中高風險 NMIBC 約佔 NMIBC 患者人口的 40%，在初始診斷後五年內有較高的疾病進展至更具侵略性的 MIBC 機率。中風險疾病患者約佔總 NMIBC 診斷的 30%。

高風險 NMIBC 的當前治療通常涉及 TURBT 後進行膀胱內（IVE）BCG 治療以誘導抗腫瘤免疫反應。此治療方案已顯示治療效益，約有 70% 的患者在初始誘導治療後達到完全緩解（CR）。然而，約有 50% 的這些患者會經歷腫瘤復發，且對於對 BCG 治療無反應的患者，治療選擇有限。雖然根治性膀胱切除術是目前對 BCG 無反應 NMIBC 的指南推薦治療，但僅約 6% 的 NMIBC 患者選擇進行膀胱切除術，考慮到此手術帶來的重大社會、功能及情緒負擔。進一步複雜化 NMIBC 患者治療選擇的是持續的 BCG 短缺，這已限制了患者資格僅限於高風險 BCG 未接觸 NMIBC。即使在這些患者中，美國新診斷、BCG 合格、治療未接觸的患者中，仍可能有大量患者未獲得足夠的 BCG 治療，甚至完全未接受治療。此外，中風險 NMIBC 患者可能因短缺而無法獲得 BCG，儘管早期輔助 BCG 治療可能帶來治療效益，但高風險患者根據國家綜合護理網路（NCCN）及美國泌尿科協會（AUA）與 SUO 共同發布的指南優先考慮。雖然中風險患者進展風險較低，但此患者羣體是所有風險類別中最異質化的，主要由多發性或頻繁復發的低級別病變或小於 3 公分的高級別 Ta 病變組成，這些病變常對現有膀胱內治療無反應。因此，管理標準以透過 TURBT 移除可見病變為中心，這對經歷頻繁侵入性手術以減少重複疾病復發的中風險患者而言，同樣帶來功能及情緒負擔。

對治療無反應及復發疾病的案例、患者對膀胱切除術的抗拒以及持續的 BCG 供應限制，已創造出對安全且有效的替代 NMIBC 治療藥物的重大未滿足醫療需求。除了我們在高風險及中風險 NMIBC 的註冊臨牀試驗外，我們也啟動了 CORE-008，這是一個開放標籤、多臂、多羣體的 Phase 2 臨牀試驗，旨在評估 cretostimogene 當作單一療法在高風險 BCG 曝露及 BCG 未接觸 NMIBC 患者中的安全性與有效性，以及在高風險 BCG 曝露及 BCG 無反應 NMIBC 患者中與其他藥物組合使用的安全性與有效性。BCG 曝露患者被定義為在 BCG 治療後持續、復發或進展性疾病但不具備特定疾病分類標準以被歸類為 BCG 無反應的患者。BCG 未接觸 NMIBC 被定義為未曾接受任何 BCG 治療的患者。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀以下對我們財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析，並與我們的合併財務報表及相關附註一同審閱，這些內容包含於本年度報告的其他部分。此討論包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性，包括在「前瞻性陳述與市場資料」節中所述的風險。我們的實際結果與特定事件的時間點可能與以下討論有重大差異。導致這種差異的因素包括，但不僅限於，以下所列及「風險因素」節中所述的風險。

此外，以下的討論與分析專注於我們截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日的財務結果與流動性及資本資源，包括這些年份的財務表現與狀況的年對年比較。針對2023年12月31日結業年度的討論與分析，以及2024年12月31日與2023年12月31日結業年度的財務表現與狀況的年對年比較，請參閱2024年12月31日結業年度年度報告中所包含的「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析」節，該節於2025年3月28日提交至SEC，並 herein by reference 納入參考。

本公司為一家晚期臨牀生物製藥公司，專注於開發與商業化cretostimogene grenadenorepvec（cretostimogene），一種正在研究中的腫瘤免疫療法，具有雙重作用機制，設計用以直接透過選擇性複製消除癌細胞，並透過活化抗腫瘤免疫反應間接發揮作用，作為治療廣泛膀胱癌患者的潛在基礎療法。cretostimogene目前處於臨牀開發階段，用於治療高風險及中風險非肌肉侵襲性膀胱癌（NMIBC）患者，這類患者可能達至150,000名。

我們正在評估cretostimogene作為單一療法在BOND-003 Cohort C的臨牀試驗中的安全性與有效性，這是一項持續進行的第三期臨牀試驗，針對高風險的卡介苗（BCG）無反應性NMIBC伴癌變（CIS）患者，有或無Ta/T1病變。考慮到目前核准療法的限制，這些BCG無反應性腫瘤患者的下一步治療為根治性膀胱切除術，即完全移除膀胱。此手術對患者而言具有顯著的社會、功能與情緒負擔。因此，對於有效的膀胱保留治療存在顯著未滿足的需求。我們已完成此羣組的入組，並於2025年9月報告了潛在的最佳治療數據。此試驗成為我們向美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）提交生物製品許可申請（BLA）的基礎，我們於2025年第四季啟動此申請，預計於2026年完成。cretostimogene已獲得FDA針對治療高風險BCG無反應性NMIBC伴CIS及有或無Ta或T1乳頭狀腫瘤的Fast Track與Breakthrough Therapy認可。此外，我們於2024年4月啟動BOND-003 Cohort P，這是一項探索性研究，評估cretostimogene單一療法在高風險BCG無反應性NMIBC伴僅有Ta/T1病變的患者中的應用。此羣組的初步數據於2025年AUA年會報告，潛在的最佳治療數據於2025年12月的泌尿道腫瘤學會（SUO）第26屆年會報告。根據來自國家癌症研究所監測、流行病學與結果計畫（NIH SEER）資料庫的內部研究、次級主張數據分析及管理假設，高風險BCG無反應性NMIBC羣組可能代表至多25,000名可治療患者。

我們亦進行第三期臨牀試驗，PIVOT-006，這是評估一種實驗性療法在中風險非肌肉浸潤性膀胱癌（NMIBC）患者中的首個隨機註冊試驗，評估在經尿道膀胱腫瘤切除術（TURBT）後使用輔助性cretostimogene的療效， enrolment 已於2025年第三季完成。這些中風險NMIBC患者因腫瘤頻繁復發而需重複進行膀胱腫瘤切除手術。此外，由於持續的BCG短缺，現行指南已不再建議此患者羣體使用經膀胱BCG治療。我們認為，若cretostimogene在中風險NMIBC獲准上市，有潛力成為此一前線輔助治療領域的首個療法，目前美國FDA尚無核准的選項。根據內部研究，來自NIH SEER資料庫的二次申報資料分析及管理假設，中風險NMIBC段可能代表最多50,000名可接觸患者。

此外，我們進行多項第二期臨牀試驗，以產生高風險BCG接觸及BCG未接觸患者的資料。2024年10月，我們啟動CORE-008 Cohort A，這是一項第二期臨牀試驗，針對未曾接受BCG治療的高風險NMIBC患者，包括有CIS及有或無Ta/T1病變的患者，以及僅有Ta/T1病變的患者。此Cohort的初步資料於2025年12月SUO年會報告。根據內部研究，來自NIH SEER資料庫的二次申報資料分析及管理假設，高風險BCG未接觸NMIBC段可能代表最多25,000名可接觸患者。2025年3月，我們擴展CORE-008，評估cretostimogene作為單一療法在高風險BCG接觸羣體（Cohort B）中的應用。此外，2025年4月，我們啟動第三個Cohort（Cohort CX），評估cretostimogene與gemcitabine組合在高風險BCG接觸及BCG無反應羣體中的應用。根據內部研究，來自NIH SEER資料庫的二次申報資料分析及管理假設，高風險BCG接觸NMIBC段可能代表最多50,000名可接觸患者。值得注意的是，cretostimogene與其他療法組合的潛力在第二期CORE-001臨牀試驗中評估，該試驗評估cretostimogene與檢查點抑制劑（CPI）pembrolizumab組合在高風險BCG無反應NMIBC患者中的應用。
自2010年成立以來，我們將幾乎所有資源投入於組織與僱用公司員工、商業計畫、籌集資金、建立與維護智慧財產權組合、進行研究、動物實驗、臨牀試驗、與第三方建立製造cretostimogene的協議，以及提供一般及行政支援。我們目前尚無核准上市的產品，也未從產品銷售中產生任何收入。

自成立以來，我們已產生重大營運虧損與營運現金流為負。我們的淨虧損為2025年12月31日止年度為1.61億美元，2024年12月31日止年度為8,800萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，我們累計虧損為3.79億美元。我們幾乎所有的淨虧損均來自與研究與開發計畫相關的費用，以及較少程度的與營運相關的一般及行政費用。我們預期在可預見的未來，仍將產生重大費用與營運虧損，並預期這些虧損將大幅增加，因我們持續進行cretostimogene的開發、尋求監管核准、以及可能商業化，並可能尋求發現與開發其他產品候選藥物、利用第三方製造cretostimogene、聘僱更多員工、擴張與保護智慧財產權，以及因成為上市公司而產生的額外費用。若我們獲得cretostimogene的監管核准，我們預期將產生大量費用，以發展商業化能力，支持產品銷售、行銷與分銷。由於藥物開發涉及眾多風險與不確定性，我們無法準確預測費用增加的時間或金額，以及何時、或是否能實現或維持盈利。即使我們能產生產品銷售，我們也可能無法實現盈利。若我們無法實現盈利或無法持續維持盈利，則我們可能無法維持預期的營運規模，並可能被迫減縮或終止營運。

截至2025年12月31日，本公司透過首次公開發行、2024年12月追加發行以及公開市場銷售協議，出售普通股股票所收到的總毛資金約為1.1 十億美元。此外，截至2025年12月31日，本公司已確認根據授權與合作協議所產生的授權與合作收入為26.9 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司持有現金、現金等價物及市場可交易證券為742.2 百萬美元，此數字不包含2025年12月31日後，根據Jefferies Sales Agreement出售3,623,101股普通股所收到的淨資金188.0 百萬美元。本公司產生任何產品收入的能力，特別是產生足夠產品收入以達成獲利的能力，將取決於cretostimogene以及任何未來產品候選品的開發與最終商業化是否成功。

2025年2月，本公司全資子公司SafeGuard Healthcare, LLC（SafeGuard）透過可轉換貸款協議（Note）從SP Healthcare SPV I, LLC（SPV）取得初始本金為25.0 百萬美元的應收款。SPV使用貸款資金投資Biovire，以協助Biovire取得提供cretostimogene臨牀供應的合同製造組織的 substantially all 資產。2025年7月20日，因SkyPath對SPV及Biovire的服務中止（Conversion Event），貸款轉換為可轉換貸款，本公司透過子公司SafeGuard取得SPV及Biovire的控制權。此控制權變更導致Biovire的營運自轉換生效日開始納入合併財務報表。
我們認為，根據目前營運計畫，現有現金、現金等價物及市場性證券將足以資助我們至少十二個月的營運，自本年度報告日算起。然而，我們的估計基於可能錯誤的假設，且營運計畫可能因許多未知因素而改變。此外，我們可能在預期時間前使用現有資金資源。

除非我們成功完成臨牀開發並取得監管批准，否則我們不會從cretostimogene或任何未來產品候選品的產品銷售中產生收入，而我們預期此過程將耗時數年，甚至可能永遠無法實現。因此，我們需要大量額外資金來支持持續營運及追求成長策略。在能從產品銷售產生顯著收入之前，我們預期將透過股票發行、債務融資或其他資金來源，包括現有或潛在未來的合作、授權及其他類似安排來資助營運。然而，我們可能無法在有利條件下或完全無法籌措額外資金或進入這些協議或安排。如果我們無法在需要時籌措資金或進入這些協議或安排，我們可能延遲、限制、減少或終止產品開發或未來商業化努力，或讓出開發與行銷產品候選品的權利，而這些我們原本希望自行開發與行銷，甚至可能停止營運。

除了製造並進行釋放測試的Biovire外，我們不擁有或經營任何製造設施，目前也沒有計畫建立任何製造設施。我們依賴，並預期持續依賴Biovire及第三方製造cretostimogene用於臨牀測試，以及在取得市場批准後進行商業製造。此外，我們依賴第三方進行cretostimogene的包裝、標籤、儲存及運輸，並預期在取得市場批准後依賴第三方進行商業產品的運作。我們認為此策略使我們能維持更高效的基礎設施，避免投資自有製造設施、設備及人力，同時也能讓我們專注於cretostimogene的開發。

headings: 與我們產品候選藥物之開發及監管核准相關之風險
Cretostimogene 基於一種用於癌症治療之創新方法，使其難以預測產品候選藥物之開發時間及成本，以及隨後取得監管核准之時間，若能取得則更難預測。
本公司尚未完成提交新藥申請（BLA）之程序，且本公司可能無法為 Cretostimogene 或任何未來產品候選藥物完成提交新藥申請（BLA）之程序。
我們正在開發 Cretostimogene 並與其他療法組合使用，此舉使我們面臨額外風險。
Cretostimogene 或任何未來產品候選藥物之製造或配方方法之變更，可能導致額外成本或延遲。
paragraphs: 您應謹慎考量下列風險因素，並配合本年度財務報告中其他資訊，包括我們的合併財務報表及相關附註，以及「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」，在做出投資本公司證券之決定前。我們無法保證下列風險因素中所討論之任何事件不會發生。這些風險可能對我們的業務、營運結果、財務狀況與成長前景造成重大且不利的影響。若發生此類情況，本公司普通股之交易價格可能會下跌。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定因素，目前我們尚未知悉，或認為不重要，也可能影響我們的業務營運或財務狀況。在本節中，我們首先提供我們所面臨的主要風險與不確定因素之總結，然後提供完整的風險因素並詳細討論。
目前我們完全依賴cretostimogene之成功，而cretostimogene為我們唯一之產品候選藥物。若我們無法推進cretostimogene進行臨牀開發、取得監管核准並最終商業化cretostimogene，或遭遇顯著延誤，將對我們的業務造成重大損害。
目前我們僅有單一產品候選藥物cretostimogene，該藥物目前處於第三期臨牀開發階段。我們目前的業務完全依賴我們成功開發、取得監管核准並及時商業化cretostimogene之能力。這可能使投資本公司之風險高於擁有多重產品候選藥物且處於積極開發中之類似公司，並可能更有效地應對主要產品候選藥物延誤或失敗之情況。cretostimogene之成功將取決於多種因素，包括以下各項：
• 成功啟動並招募臨牀試驗參與者，並完成臨牀試驗且結果良好，包括持續進行之cretostimogene第三期臨牀試驗之完整數據讀取；
• 美國FDA或相應外國監管機構接受cretostimogene臨牀試驗之監管申請，以及接受我們所提出之cretostimogene計畫臨牀試驗設計；
• 在臨牀試驗與前期臨牀研究中觀察到的不良事件之頻率與嚴重程度；
